sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I would say we're going to do four episodes on Baghdad, the story of how it comes to be founded, its golden age, the legends that surround it.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们要分四集来讲述巴格达，讲述它如何建立、它的黄金时代以及围绕它的传说。

sentences.en: I would say that these episodes are as influential on global history as any episodes we've done.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些集数对全球历史的影响力，不亚于我们做过的任何一期节目。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 因为这是世界历史中一个巨大的转折点。

sentences.en: We're looking back a little bit.

sentences.zh: 但这也是伊斯兰教自我意识的发展。

sentences.en: It's also the way in which the center of gravity of the Islamic world moves, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也是伊斯兰世界重心转移的方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because the Arabs have come out of the desert.
sentences.zh: 因为阿拉伯人从沙漠中走出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: And in both of those, we were exploring the way in which the legends that are told about Muhammad, the origins of Islam, the emergence of the Islamic empire, how hard it can be
sentences.zh: 在那两期节目中，我们都在探索关于穆罕默德的传说、伊斯兰教的起源、伊斯兰帝国的崛起，以及要将这些传说

sentences.zh: 但我认为我们在那些节目中提出的核心论点是，伊斯兰教并非一蹴而就，就像雅典娜从……

sentences.zh: 伊斯兰教的第一个伟大帝国王朝——倭马亚王朝（Umayyads）被推翻，取而代之的是一个新的王朝——阿拔斯王朝（Abbasids）。

sentences.zh: 一个标点符号，标志着那个过渡过程，即伊斯兰教从古代、从罗马和波斯世界中脱颖而出的过程。

sentences.en: antiquity, from the Roman and the Persian worlds.

sentences.en: And they come to power after four commanders of the faithful, four caliphs who will be commemorated by Islamic tradition as the Rashidun, the righteously guided.
sentences.zh: 因为他们第一次开始遭遇军事挫折。

sentences.en: So that's Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali.
sentences.zh: 732年，一支向北进入法兰克领土，前往图尔圣马丁大教堂的突袭部队被击败了。

sentences.en: And Ali is a key figure in this story because he is both the cousin and the son-in-law of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 在伊斯兰世界的另一端，在河中地区（Transoxania），即接近中国的地方，伊斯兰军队在717年的一场名为阿克苏（Aksu）的战役中被击败。

sentences.en: He rules as a caliph, but he ends up assassinated and he leaves behind children.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着他们失去了河中北部地区。

sentences.en: And the question of what the role of his bloodline should be is going to be a kind of key part of this story.
sentences.zh: 当然，哈里发国面临的最大敌人是罗马帝国的残余，其首都在君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: But before we come to all that, by the 740s, although the Ameyads are the masters of this vast empire, there is a kind of growing
sentences.zh: 倭马亚人曾两次试图攻占它。

sentences.en: mood of crisis because for the first time they're starting to experience military reverses.
sentences.zh: 在674年，以及716年至717年，他们对这座伟大的凯撒之城进行了大规模的两栖入侵，但它坚守住了。

sentences.en: So in 732, a raiding party going northwards into the land of the Franks up to the great shrine of St. Martin in Tor is defeated.
sentences.zh: 因此，在随后的几十年里，开始出现归于先知的言论，称拜占庭永远不会陷落，称罗马人……

sentences.en: At the opposite end of the Islamic world in Transoxania, so approaching China, the armies of Islam are defeated a battle called Aksu in 717.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: And that basically means that they lose northern Transoxania.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: The greatest enemy, of course, faced by the caliphate is the surviving rump of the Roman empire with its capital in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: And the Ameyads have twice tried to capture it.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: So in 674, and then again in 716 to 717, vast amphibious invasions of the great city of the Caesars, but it holds out.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: And so in the decades that follow, you start to get sayings that are attributed to the prophet saying that Byzantium will never fall, that the people of Rum
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处中断，译文对应完整）

sentences.en: are like rock and water.
sentences.zh: 就像岩石与流水。

sentences.en: They will be with you till the end of time.
sentences.zh: 它们将伴随你直到时间的尽头。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is bad for the Ameyad reputation because their legitimacy to a degree has been founded on a sense of their invincibility.
sentences.zh: 这对倭马亚王朝的声誉非常不利，因为他们的合法性在某种程度上建立在一种不可战胜感之上。

sentences.en: So up to that point, Tom, had they envisaged themselves as living in a sort of a unipolar
sentences.zh: 所以在那之前，汤姆，他们是否曾设想过自己生活在一个单极世界中，

sentences.en: world where they would be the only super bearer and now they have to accept that every empire
sentences.zh: 在这个世界里他们是唯一的超级大国，而现在他们不得不接受这样一个事实：每个帝国

sentences.en: has its limits and they have theirs and they have to accept that there are going to be other
sentences.zh: 都有其局限性，他们也有自己的局限性，他们必须接受未来还会有其他的

sentences.en: geopolitical powers, you know, they're Romans or whoever, and they have to live within those boundaries.
sentences.zh: 地缘政治力量，你知道，无论是罗马人还是其他人，他们必须在这些边界内生存。

sentences.en: I think they continue to hope that they will conquer Byzantium and that the conquest will continue.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们仍然希望能够征服拜占庭，并且征服会继续下去。

sentences.en: But there is definitely a sense that perhaps the conquest of the world isn't going to be quite as easy as they had assumed in the kind of heady days when it seemed
sentences.zh: 但确实有一种感觉，也许征服世界并不像他们在那些意气风发的日子里所设想的那样容易，当时似乎

sentences.en: that God was giving them victories wherever they went.
sentences.zh: 上帝在他们所到之处都赐予他们胜利。

sentences.en: So there's trouble on the frontiers.
sentences.zh: 所以边境出现了麻烦。

sentences.en: At the same time, there are all kinds of sectarian conflicts going on within Islam itself.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，伊斯兰教内部也发生了各种各样的宗派冲突。

sentences.en: And these date back to the reign of Ali, which we talked about.
sentences.zh: 这些冲突可以追溯到我们之前谈到的阿里统治时期。

sentences.en: So that's back in the 7th century.
sentences.zh: 也就是回到公元7世纪。

sentences.en: So the guy who was assassinated.
sentences.zh: 就是那个被暗杀的人。

sentences.en: The guy who was assassinated.
sentences.zh: 那个被暗杀的人。

sentences.en: The cousin and the son-in-law of the prophet.
sentences.zh: 先知的堂弟兼女婿。

sentences.en: So the people who are responsible for Ali's assassination, this is a group of people called the Karajites, which literally mean those who go out.
sentences.zh: 那么，对阿里遇刺负责的人，是一群被称为“哈瓦利吉派”的人，字面意思是“出走者”。

sentences.en: And these are people who, they're in Ali's army.
sentences.zh: 这些人，他们原本在阿里的军队里。

sentences.en: They feel that Ali is basically a heretic, that he is not measuring up to the high standards
sentences.zh: 他们觉得阿里本质上是个异端，他没有达到他们所期望的高标准，

sentences.en: that they would expect from a Muslim, let alone a blood relative and marriage relative of the prophet.
sentences.zh: 更不用说作为先知的血亲和姻亲所应具备的标准了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What's he doing?
sentences.zh: 他在做什么？

sentences.en: Because the Karajites are looking, are reading the Quran, which preaches a very radical kind of egalitarianism.
sentences.zh: 因为哈瓦利吉派在阅读《古兰经》，而《古兰经》宣扬一种非常激进的平等主义。

sentences.en: Justice and equality are very, very fundamental to the moral teachings of the
sentences.zh: 正义与平等是《古兰经》道德教义中非常、非常根本的原则。

sentences.en: Quran.
sentences.zh: 《古兰经》。

sentences.en: And they argue that actually, you know, the true aristocracy in Islam should be one of piety, not of blood.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，实际上，伊斯兰教中真正的贵族地位应该基于虔诚，而不是血统。

sentences.en: And therefore, if a slave is more devoted to God than, say, the cousin of Muhammad, then he is more righteous.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果一个奴隶比穆罕默德的堂弟更虔诚地侍奉上帝，那么他就是更正义的。

sentences.en: And this is a notion that Ali is not prepared to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 而这是阿里无法容忍的观念。

sentences.en: And so he kind of expels them from his army.
sentences.zh: 于是他把他们从军队中驱逐了出去。

sentences.en: And the Karajites are, I mean, to the degree that you can find forebears of the Islamic state in the 7th century or the 8th century, I mean, it's kind of very
sentences.zh: 哈瓦利吉派，我的意思是，如果说在7世纪或8世纪能找到伊斯兰国的先驱，虽然这样说有点

sentences.en: anachronistic to say so, but the Karajites would be the parallel.
sentences.zh: 时代错乱，但哈瓦利吉派确实与之相似。

sentences.en: They are very, very brutal.
sentences.zh: 他们非常、非常残暴。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of stories of them slicing open the bellies of those whom they condemn as infidels.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的故事讲述他们剖开那些被他们定为异教徒的人的肚子。

sentences.en: They go into marketplaces cloaked with swords hidden underneath their cloaks.
sentences.zh: 他们走进市场，斗篷下藏着剑。

sentences.en: They'll draw the swords out and just kind of turn and turn like whirling dervishes, killing as many people as they can until they're killed.
sentences.zh: 他们会拔出剑，像旋转的苦行僧一样不停地转动，杀死尽可能多的人，直到自己被杀。

sentences.en: So very, very kind of intimidating, frightening figures, a kind of murderous piety.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是非常令人胆寒、可怕的人物，一种杀戮式的虔诚。

sentences.en: And Ali sees them as the dangerous opponents to sane rule that they are.
sentences.zh: 阿里视他们为理智统治的危险对手。

sentences.en: And he militarily crushes them in 658.
sentences.zh: 他在658年从军事上粉碎了他们。

sentences.en: But then three years later, one of them succeeds in murdering him.
sentences.zh: 但三年后，其中一人成功谋杀了他。

sentences.en: While he's at prayers in the great city of Kufa, which is a kind of the equivalent of a Roman legionary base.
sentences.zh: 当时他正在伟大的库法城祈祷，那相当于罗马军团的基地。

sentences.en: It's a great military base for the Arabs built on the borders of Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 那是阿拉伯人为建立在美索不达米亚边界上的一座伟大的军事基地。

sentences.en: So what's now Iraq?
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的伊拉克？

sentences.en: That's quite close to where, not that a million miles away from where they will end up founding
sentences.zh: 那离他们最终建立巴格达的地方很近，不是吗？

sentences.en: Baghdad, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，就在那个角落。

sentences.en: It's absolutely that kind of, that corner, yes.
sentences.zh: 绝对是那个角落，是的。

sentences.en: And Kufa will play a very important part because there are lots and lots of Karajites inside Kufa.
sentences.zh: 库法将发挥非常重要的作用，因为库法城内有大量哈瓦利吉派成员。

sentences.en: It's a kind of breeding ground for radicalism.
sentences.zh: 它是激进主义的温床。

sentences.en: But there are other radicals as well in Kufa going through the Amayad period, right the way into the 8th century.
sentences.zh: 但在整个倭马亚时期，一直到8世纪，库法还有其他激进分子。

sentences.en: And the most significant of these are kind of the opposites of the Karajites.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的一派可以说是哈瓦利吉派的对立面。

sentences.en: The Karajites reject Ali's claim to be the legitimate heir of Muhammad because they say he's not pious enough.
sentences.zh: 哈瓦利吉派拒绝承认阿里作为穆罕默德合法继承人的主张，因为他们说他不够虔诚。

sentences.en: But there are those who say that Islam can only be ruled by the heirs of Ali.
sentences.zh: 但也有人认为伊斯兰教只能由阿里的继承人来统治。

sentences.en: And these people become known as the Shia Ali, the Shia Ali.
sentences.zh: 这些人被称为“阿里党人”，即什叶派。

sentences.en: So these are the Shia, Shia MusliMs. They're still with us to this day.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是什叶派，什叶派穆斯林。他们至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: And these are people in the 7th century who believe that Ali's sons, who are obviously also the grandsons of the prophet should rule.
sentences.zh: 这些人生活在7世纪，他们相信阿里的儿子们，也就是先知的外孙们，应该统治。

sentences.en: These grandsons are denied the rule of the caliphate by the Amayads.
sentences.zh: 这些外孙被倭马亚王朝剥夺了哈里发的统治权。

sentences.en: One of them is killed at Karbala.
sentences.zh: 其中一人在卡尔巴拉被杀。

sentences.en: Again, still a great place of pilgrimage outside what is now Baghdad for the Shia.
sentences.zh: 那里至今仍是什叶派在现今巴格达郊外的一处伟大的朝圣地。

sentences.en: And the Amayads have every stake in crushing the Shia as they do the Karajites.
sentences.zh: 倭马亚王朝像镇压哈瓦利吉派一样，有充分的理由镇压什叶派。

sentences.en: But the Shia remain.
sentences.zh: 但什叶派依然存在。

sentences.en: And they kind of basically take a leaf out of the Sasanian books.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上借鉴了萨珊王朝的做法。

sentences.en: So you remember I said that the conviction of
sentences.zh: 还记得我说过，萨珊帝国中琐罗亚斯德教徒的信念是，

sentences.en: Zoroastrians in the Sasanian Empire is that the Sasanian royal dynasty are essentially divinely appointed, that this is a divinely sanctioned bloodline.
sentences.zh: 萨珊皇室本质上是神授的，这是一个受神圣认可的血统。

sentences.en: This is Persia, right?
sentences.zh: 这是波斯，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That conviction essentially migrates to the descendants of Ali.
sentences.zh: 这种信念本质上转移到了阿里的后裔身上。

sentences.en: So Tom, is that why to this day, Persia, aka Iran, is a hotbed of Shia or Shiites as people might call them?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，这就是为什么直到今天，波斯，也就是伊朗，是什叶派的温床吗？

sentences.en: No, it becomes Shiite much later, I think in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为它在很久之后，即16世纪才成为什叶派国家。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But you could, I mean, it has been argued that there is a kind of implicit buried Zoroastrianism that fuses with Shiism that does perhaps explain it.
sentences.zh: 但你可以说，有人认为有一种隐含的、深埋的琐罗亚斯德教与什叶派融合，这或许能解释这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a very complicated territory.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的领域。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think the key thing is that at this point, these various factions, these various sectarian divisions are still very much alive.
sentences.zh: 我认为关键在于，在这一点上，这些不同的派系、这些不同的宗派分裂仍然非常活跃。

sentences.en: They're kind of fusing.
sentences.zh: 它们正在融合。

sentences.en: So in the, again, under the Umayyads, there's a kind of brilliant figure who gets thrown up.
sentences.zh: 所以，在倭马亚王朝统治下，出现了一个非常出众的人物。

sentences.en: This is the process of civil wars that sees Abdul Malik, the great Umayyad caliph, who ends up building the Dome of the Rock.
sentences.zh: 这是内战过程中的一幕，见证了伟大的倭马亚哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克，他最终建造了圆顶清真寺。

sentences.en: While he is busy establishing his rule in Syria, this figure appears in Iraq, who is commemorated
sentences.zh: 当他忙于在叙利亚建立统治时，伊拉克出现了这样一个人，他被纪念为

sentences.en: as Muqtah, the deceiver, who seizes the treasury in Kufar, gives it all away to the poor.
sentences.zh: “穆赫塔尔”，即欺骗者，他夺取了库法的国库，并将其全部分发给穷人。

sentences.en: So again, you see this kind of sense of radical egalitarianism, the sense that the poor can
sentences.zh: 所以你再次看到了这种激进的平等主义意识，即穷人可以向富人要求正义，

sentences.en: claim justice from the rich, urging a revolution, saying that all men should be equal, claiming to be a prophet and huge excitement because he has, Dominic, a magic chair.
sentences.zh: 他煽动革命，声称人人平等，自称是先知，并引起了巨大的轰动，因为他有一把神奇的椅子，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Oh, crikey.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Which he parades around.
sentences.zh: 他带着它到处游行。

sentences.en: I love a magic chair.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢神奇的椅子。

sentences.en: Like the wishing chair in Ina Blyton, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像伊妮德·布莱顿书里的许愿椅一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So he's a kind of tremendous figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个了不起的人物。

sentences.en: And it's said by his supporters that he's accompanied by angels on horses of fire.
sentences.zh: 他的支持者说，他有骑着火马的天使陪伴。

sentences.en: Actually, his followers are kind of terrifying cudgel bearers, they're called.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他的追随者是一群被称为“棍棒手”的可怕之徒。

sentences.en: And they end up kind of beating everyone up.
sentences.zh: 他们最终到处殴打别人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this sense that militant piety can shade into extreme violence is a continuing theme throughout this period.
sentences.zh: 所以这种激进的虔诚可能演变成极端暴力的感觉，是贯穿这一时期的持续主题。

sentences.en: And it explains actually why a Mayad rule comes to be welcomed.
sentences.zh: 这也解释了为什么倭马亚王朝的统治最终受到欢迎。

sentences.en: So Muqtah, the deceiver, ends up killed.
sentences.zh: 所以“欺骗者”穆赫塔尔最终被杀。

sentences.en: His severed hand is nailed to the mosque in Kufar.
sentences.zh: 他被砍下的手被钉在库法的清真寺上。

sentences.en: His chair is burned.
sentences.zh: 他的椅子被烧毁了。

sentences.en: But he comes to be revered by the Shia as a supporter of Ali.
sentences.zh: 但他作为阿里的支持者，后来受到什叶派的尊崇。

sentences.en: And in the 740s, you have a whole kind of renewal of Karajite uprisings, of Shia uprisings, because these are people who are looking at the military defeats on the frontiers,
sentences.zh: 在740年代，你看到了一整套哈瓦利吉派起义和什叶派起义的复兴，因为这些人看着边境上的军事失败，

sentences.en: looking at the wealth and the splendor of the Mayad caliphs and saying, these are un-Islamic figures.
sentences.zh: 看着倭马亚哈里发的财富和辉煌，说：这些人不是真正的伊斯兰统治者。

sentences.en: God does not favor them.
sentences.zh: 上帝并不偏爱他们。

sentences.en: He wants a new dispensation.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个新的秩序。

sentences.en: And in 745, the Karajites actually proclaimed their own caliph and managed to secure a big kind of chunk of Iraq.
sentences.zh: 745年，哈瓦利吉派甚至宣布了他们自己的哈里发，并成功控制了伊拉克的一大片地区。

sentences.en: So none of this is good for the Mayads.
sentences.zh: 所以这对倭马亚王朝来说都不是好事。

sentences.en: But I think it would have been manageable for them if it wasn't for the fact that something
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果不是因为发生了另一件事，这对他们来说本来是可以控制的，

sentences.en: else is also happening, which will in the long run be terminal for the Mayads themselves, but even more seismically, be hugely influential on the growth and development of Islam.
sentences.zh: 这件事从长远来看对倭马亚王朝本身是致命的，但更具震撼性的是，它对伊斯兰教的成长和发展产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And essentially, it's a process that will culminate in the development of the kind of Islam that is by far the largest form, what we call Sunni Islam.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这是一个最终导致伊斯兰教发展出目前最大流派的过程，也就是我们所说的逊尼派伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: And I think we should maybe take a break now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在也许该休息一下了。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we can look at exactly what Sunni Islam is, how it develops, and exactly
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们可以看看逊尼派伊斯兰教究竟是什么，它是如何发展的，以及为什么它对倭马亚王朝如此具有威胁性，

sentences.en: why it's so menacing for the Mayads and the role that it will come to play in the revolution that overthrows the Mayads and brings the Abbasids to power.
sentences.zh: 以及它在推翻倭马亚王朝并使阿拔斯王朝上台的革命中将发挥的作用。

sentences.en: We'll find out more after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息后我们会了解更多。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: That flight with 350 passengers.
sentences.zh: 那架载有350名乘客的航班。

sentences.en: The great game.
sentences.zh: 大博弈。

sentences.en: Strategic struggle between Britain and Russia.
sentences.zh: 英国与俄罗斯之间的战略斗争。

sentences.en: We assess our prime minister.
sentences.zh: 我们评估我们的首相。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.

sentences.en: So, we have been in what is now Iraq.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在现在的伊拉克。

sentences.en: We're eventually going to get to the founding of the great city of Baghdad.
sentences.zh: 我们最终会谈到伟大城市巴格达的建立。

sentences.en: But we're setting, very carefully setting out the context for it.
sentences.zh: 但我们正在非常仔细地为它铺陈背景。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we've been talking about the Umayyad dynasty.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，我们一直在谈论倭马亚王朝。

sentences.en: They're based in Damascus, in Syria.
sentences.zh: 他们的基地位于叙利亚的大马士革。

sentences.en: They're presiding over this empire that is very fractious.
sentences.zh: 他们统治着这个极其分裂的帝国。

sentences.en: They've suffered a series of defeats.
sentences.zh: 他们遭受了一连串的失败。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of sectarian, millenarian movements that are challenging their authority.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的宗派运动和千禧年主义运动都在挑战他们的权威。

sentences.en: But you said before the break that this might have been manageable were it not for this development a long way away.
sentences.zh: 但你在休息前提到，如果不是因为远方发生的这一变故，这种情况本是可以控制的。

sentences.en: So, we're going to get to that, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要谈谈那个变故，对吧？

sentences.en: But do you want to talk a bit about the kind of people that the Umayyads are ruling?
sentences.zh: 但你想聊聊倭马亚王朝统治下的人民吗？

sentences.en: The kind of, the population whose support they need?
sentences.zh: 那种他们需要争取支持的民众？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, I think there's always a temptation when you think of the coming of Islam.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在思考伊斯兰教兴起时，人们总是容易产生一种错觉。

sentences.en: You think, you know, there's the Romans and the Persians and then the Arabs conquer it.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，你知道，先是罗马人和波斯人，然后阿拉伯人征服了这里。

sentences.en: And basically everyone in the Middle East becomes Muslim.
sentences.zh: 接着中东的所有人基本上都变成了穆斯林。

sentences.en: This is absolutely not the case.
sentences.zh: 事实完全不是这样。

sentences.en: The Arabs are a very tiny minority, ruling lands that are absolutely teeming with different peoples, with different traditions, and perhaps most importantly,
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯人只是极少数，他们统治的土地上挤满了不同民族、不同传统的人，而最重要的是，

sentences.en: with different understandings of the divine.
sentences.zh: 他们对神有着不同的理解。

sentences.en: So, if you look at the heartlands of the caliphate, so Syria, Palestine, Egypt, the lands that had been ruled by the Romans, and Iraq and Iran,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你看看哈里发帝国的核心地带，也就是叙利亚、巴勒斯坦、埃及这些曾由罗马人统治的土地，以及伊拉克和伊朗，

sentences.en: the lands that had been ruled by the Persians, by the Sasanians.
sentences.zh: 那些曾由波斯人、萨珊王朝统治的土地。

sentences.en: The largest number of people there are Christians.
sentences.zh: 那里人数最多的是基督徒。

sentences.en: This is a very, very Christian world in the 7th and 8th centuries.
sentences.zh: 在七、八世纪，这是一个非常、非常基督教化的世界。

sentences.en: They're obviously dominant in the former Roman provinces, but there are also an awful lot of them in the former Sasanian Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们显然在前罗马帝国行省占主导地位，但在前萨珊帝国境内也有大量基督徒。

sentences.en: So, there were a lot of Christians in Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 所以，美索不达米亚有很多基督徒。

sentences.en: You also, of course, have the Zoroastrians, who we mentioned in the first half.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有我们在上半场提到的琐罗亚斯德教徒（祆教徒）。

sentences.en: For them, the overthrow of the Sasanians is devastating, because they had seen the Sasanian dynasty as a kind of a pledge that God was on their side.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，萨珊王朝的覆灭是毁灭性的，因为他们一直将萨珊王朝视为上帝站在他们一边的某种保证。

sentences.en: So, dare I say, the sacral quality of the Sasanian bloodline.
sentences.zh: 所以，我敢说，萨珊王朝血统具有某种神圣的特质。

sentences.en: But Tom, a quick question.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，问个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Why is that more devastating for the people in the old Persian Empire, the Zoroastrians, than the loss of their territory is for the Christians in the former Roman Empire?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对旧波斯帝国的琐罗亚斯德教徒来说，比失去领土对前罗马帝国的基督徒来说更具毁灭性？

sentences.en: Is it because the Christians, they didn't need to be in an officially Christian state, because they had a different conception of…
sentences.zh: 是因为基督徒不需要生活在一个官方的基督教国家，因为他们有不同的……观念吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because Christians have flourished in Mesopotamia, despite the fact that it's a Zoroastrian king ruling Iran and Iraq.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管统治伊朗和伊拉克的是琐罗亚斯德教国王，基督徒在美索不达米亚依然繁荣发展。

sentences.en: They don't have to worry about it.
sentences.zh: 他们不必为此担心。

sentences.en: And it doesn't, you know, Christianity flourished long before Constantine converted to Christianity and before the Roman emperors became Christian.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，基督教在君士坦丁皈依之前，在罗马皇帝成为基督徒之前，就已经繁荣了很久。

sentences.en: So, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以，这没问题。

sentences.en: There's a kind of, if you want to put it in anachronistic terms, there's a division between church and state for Christians, even in late antiquity.
sentences.zh: 如果用时代错乱的术语来说，即使在古典时代晚期，基督徒内部也存在一种政教分离。

sentences.en: But there is no real division between church and state in the Persian world.
sentences.zh: 但在波斯世界，政教之间并没有真正的分离。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, the loss of the Sasanian dynasty is completely devastating.
sentences.zh: 因此，萨珊王朝的覆灭是彻底的毁灭。

sentences.en: So, we have a Zoroastrian priest in the wake of the Arab conquests mourning the faith is ruined.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们看到一位琐罗亚斯德教祭司在阿拉伯征服后哀叹信仰已毁。

sentences.en: The Shah and Shah, so the king of kings, he was slain like a dog.
sentences.zh: 万王之王，也就是众王之王，像狗一样被杀死了。

sentences.en: And the two are kind of, you know, he's equating the two.
sentences.zh: 他们两人，你知道，他把这两者等同起来了。

sentences.en: The loss of the Sasanian dynasty means that the faith is ruined.
sentences.zh: 萨珊王朝的覆灭意味着信仰的毁灭。

sentences.en: And there's a further tragedy for the Zoroastrians, which is that in the Quran,
sentences.zh: 对琐罗亚斯德教徒来说，还有一个更深层的悲剧，那就是在《古兰经》中，

sentences.en: it's specified that those who follow the teachings of the prophet should allow the peoples of the book, as long as they acknowledge the supremacy of Islam,
sentences.zh: 明确规定追随先知教诲的人应该允许“有经人”存在，只要他们承认伊斯兰教的至高地位，

sentences.en: as long as they pay a tax called the Jizya, they should be allowed the freedom to worship as they please.
sentences.zh: 只要他们缴纳一种叫“吉兹亚”（人丁税）的税，就应该允许他们自由地进行礼拜。

sentences.en: And those are what?
sentences.zh: 那些人是指？

sentences.en: Jews and Christians?
sentences.zh: 犹太人和基督徒？

sentences.en: Jews and Christians and a mysterious people called the Sabaeans, who may be popping up later in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 犹太人、基督徒，还有一种神秘的民族叫萨比人，他们可能会在以后的播客中出现。

sentences.en: Nobody's entirely sure who the Sabaeans are, but the Jews and the Christians, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没人完全确定萨比人是谁，但犹太人和基督徒绝对在列。

sentences.en: So, Jews and Christians, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以，犹太人和基督徒，这没问题。

sentences.en: The Arabs do not go around kind of destroying synagogues or churches.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯人不会到处去破坏犹太会堂或教堂。

sentences.en: They respect them.
sentences.zh: 他们尊重这些地方。

sentences.en: But the fire temples of the Zoroastrians, fire is sacred to Zoroaster.
sentences.zh: 但琐罗亚斯德教的火神庙，火对琐罗亚斯德教徒来说是神圣的。

sentences.en: And across Iraq, across the western fringes of Iran, these start to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 在伊拉克各地，在伊朗的西部边缘，这些神庙开始被摧毁。

sentences.en: And it's actually only in the very remote regions of Khorasan, so northeastern Iran, that the fire temples survive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，只有在呼罗珊的偏远地区，也就是伊朗东北部，火神庙才得以幸存。

sentences.en: And it's possible for the Zoroastrian priesthood and Zoroastrian worshippers to continue their faith as they had done back in their heyday under the Sasanian rulers.
sentences.zh: 琐罗亚斯德教的祭司和信徒才有可能像在萨珊统治时期的全盛时代那样继续他们的信仰。

sentences.en: So you've got Christians, you've got Zoroastrians who are very, very unhappy.
sentences.zh: 所以你有基督徒，有非常、非常不满的琐罗亚斯德教徒。

sentences.en: And then you have Jews and Jews, like the Christians, are much happier.
sentences.zh: 然后你有犹太人，犹太人像基督徒一样，要快乐得多。

sentences.en: And this is a golden age of Jewish scholarship.
sentences.zh: 这是一个犹太学术的黄金时代。

sentences.en: So you have Jews in Palestine who are great scholars, but the greatest centers of Jewish scholarship, towns called Surah and Pompadita in Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦有伟大的犹太学者，但最伟大的犹太学术中心是美索不达米亚的苏拉和庞贝迪塔。

sentences.en: These are where the rabbis are developing the Talmud.
sentences.zh: 拉比们就是在那里编纂《塔木德》的。

sentences.en: And the Talmud is a vast kind of sprawling edifice of legal commentary.
sentences.zh: 《塔木德》是一部庞大而错综复杂的法律注释汇编。

sentences.en: And then it's legal commentary on legal commentary on legal commentary, textual analysis, commentary on Torah.
sentences.zh: 它是对法律的注释，再对注释进行注释，还有文本分析，以及对《托拉》的解读。

sentences.en: In these great Jewish centers of scholarship, you have the idea of teachings from God that are preserved in Torah,
sentences.zh: 在这些伟大的犹太学术中心，有一种观念认为上帝的教诲保存在《托拉》中，

sentences.en: that have literally come from God, that have been written by God on the tablets of stone brought down from Sinai by Moses.
sentences.zh: 这些教诲确实来自上帝，是上帝写在石板上，由摩西从西奈山带下来的。

sentences.en: But you also have this other idea that there is a kind of vast legal complex that can be analyzed by these rabbis
sentences.zh: 但你也有另一种观念，认为存在一个庞大的法律体系，可以由这些拉比进行分析，

sentences.en: that is also kind of interfused with an understanding of God's purpose and the laws that he wants to govern God's people.
sentences.zh: 这个体系也融合了对上帝旨意以及他希望用来治理上帝子民的法律的理解。

sentences.en: And that sense of a written law and a spoken law is the kind of the great cultural innovation
sentences.zh: 那种成文法和口传法的意识，是拉比们在古典时代晚期，特别是在美索不达米亚发展出的伟大文化创新。

sentences.en: that the rabbis over the course of late antiquity in Palestine, but above all in Mesopotamia, have been developing.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些传统现在都处于阿拉伯人的统治之下，而阿拉伯人正开始发展后来成为伊斯兰教的东西。

sentences.en: And so all these traditions are now subject to the Arabs who are starting to develop what will become Islam.
sentences.zh: 在你继续之前，稍微停一下。

sentences.en: Just before you move on just a bit.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你是一个普通的基督徒或犹太人，你知道，你过着平庸的生活，是个面包师什么的。

sentences.en: So in other words, if you're an ordinary Christian or a Jew, you know, you're plodding along, you're a baker or whatever.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰教和阿拉伯帝国的到来并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: The coming of Islam and the Arab empire doesn't make any difference.
sentences.zh: 是的，感觉还行，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of fine, right?
sentences.zh: 你交一笔税，这可能很烦人。

sentences.en: You pay a tax, which has probably been annoying.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，在东罗马帝国晚期，有各种各样的争议和冲突。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, there were all kinds of, you know, controversies and bust-ups and stuff in the late Eastern Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能很高兴那些混乱消失了，现在有了一点秩序。

sentences.en: So you're probably glad that a lot of that has gone away and you've got a bit of order.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在前罗马帝国行省对基督徒的影响比对犹太人的影响更大，

sentences.en: I think it's more disruptive for Christians than it is for Jews in the former Roman provinces
sentences.zh: 因为基督徒习惯了当老板，现在他们变得和犹太人一样了。

sentences.en: because Christians were accustomed to being the bosses and now they go to being equivalent to the Jews.
sentences.zh: 犹太人过去被迫向罗马人纳税以换取信仰自由。

sentences.en: So the Jews had been forced to pay taxes to the Romans for the right to practice their faith.
sentences.zh: 现在基督徒也必须这样做。

sentences.en: And now Christians are having to do the same.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他们来说有点屈辱。

sentences.en: So it's a bit humiliating for them.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到有点愤恨。

sentences.en: They're a bit resentful of it.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这并没有伤及他们的根本。

sentences.en: But, you know, no real skin off their nose.
sentences.zh: 他们可以继续做他们做的事。

sentences.en: They can carry on doing what they do.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: It's all fine.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，基督徒仍然占绝大多数。

sentences.en: And as I say, Christians remain vastly in the majority.
sentences.zh: 这对阿拉伯人来说是个问题，因为风险在于他们会被庞大的基督徒群体所吞没。

sentences.en: And this for the Arabs is a problem because the risk is that they will be kind of swallowed up by the vast mass of Christians.
sentences.zh: 所以从一开始，阿拉伯人就非常重视将自己与被统治的民族区分开来，

sentences.en: And so it's right from the beginning, it's been important to the Arabs that they distinguish themselves from their subject peoples,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们建立库法作为军事基地，不是在美索不达米亚的核心地带，

sentences.en: which is why, for instance, they found Kufa, this great kind of military base, not in the heartlands of Mesopotamia,
sentences.zh: 而是在沙漠边缘，这样他们就能保持，你知道，他们沙漠般的纯洁性。

sentences.en: but right on the desert borders so that they can kind of preserve, you know, their desert purity, if you like.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能保持自己的身份。

sentences.en: That they can maintain their identity.
sentences.zh: 因为在早期伊斯兰教中，人们认为阿拉伯人像犹太人一样，在血缘上是亚伯拉罕的后裔。

sentences.en: And because in early Islam, there is a sense that the Arabs, like the Jews, are descended by blood from Abraham.
sentences.zh: 亚伯拉罕有两个儿子。

sentences.en: So Abraham has two sons.
sentences.zh: 一个是以撒，犹太人声称是他的后裔；另一个是以实玛利，阿拉伯人声称是他的后裔。

sentences.en: He has Isaac, from whom the Jews claim descent, and he has Ishmael, from whom the Arabs claim descent.
sentences.zh: 所以对许多阿拉伯人来说，伊斯兰教被视为只属于阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: So for many Arabs, Islam is seen as being only for the Arabs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们绝对不希望非信徒皈依伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: So they absolutely don't want non-believers to convert to Islam.
sentences.zh: 他们想在肥沃月湾的边缘保持自己的身份。

sentences.en: They want to preserve their identity on the margins of the Fertile Crescent.
sentences.zh: 并保持他们的伊斯兰身份作为一种独特的标志。

sentences.en: And also keep their Islamic identity as something that is distinctive to them.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你是穆斯林，你会获得各种财政特权。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, you get all kinds of fiscal privileges if you're a Muslim.
sentences.zh: 犹太人、基督徒和琐罗亚斯德教徒都必须缴纳人头税和其他税款，以维持他们的信仰。

sentences.en: Jews and Christians and Zoroastrians are all having to pay poll taxes and taxes that will enable them to continue practicing their faiths.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你成为穆斯林，就可以免除这些。

sentences.en: So if you become a Muslim, you get out of that.
sentences.zh: 但阿拉伯人意识到，这是一种他们必须防范的骗局。

sentences.en: But the Arabs are aware that, you know, this is a scam that they have to guard againSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们用各种屈辱的条件来限制皈依。

sentences.en: And so they, you know, they hedge conversion about with all kinds of indignities.
sentences.zh: 所以犹太人、琐罗亚斯德教徒或基督徒仅仅顺从上帝是不够的。

sentences.en: So it's not enough for a Jew or a Zoroastrian or a Christian to submit to God.
sentences.zh: 他还必须顺从一位阿拉伯赞助人。

sentences.en: the war between the Umayyads and the Abbasids, the great Abbasid revolution.

sentences.en: And then at last, we'll get back to where we started with the foundation of the great city of peace, the round city of Baghdad, the greatest city at that point in human history.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们将回到我们开始的地方，即伟大的和平之城——圆形的巴格达城的建立，那是当时人类历史上最伟大的城市。

sentences.en: to the Rest is History, but you're not really part of the elite, then you'll just have to wait until Thursday.

sentences.en: But I hope it'll be worth waiting for because the story of the Abbasid revolution is a brilliant, brilliant narrative.

sentences.en: And then the founding of Baghdad, very, very romantic, epical moment in world history.

sentences.zh: 所以，非常非常令人激动。

sentences.zh: 这故事再精彩不过了。
